Vulnerability Management

Preuve d’atténuation

Documented proof that specific technical or administrative actions have effectively addressed and reduced the risk of cryptographic or PKI vulnerabilities, as required by compliance or audit processes.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Preuve d’atténuation?

In this glossary, Preuve d’atténuation refers to: Documented proof that specific technical or administrative actions have effectively addressed and reduced the risk of cryptographic or PKI vulnerabilities, as required by compliance or audit processes.

How is Preuve d’atténuation used in cybersecurity?

In cybersecurity communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Les preuves d’atténuation, telles que les journaux système mis à jour et les listes de contrôle de conformité, doivent être conservées après l’application de correctifs PKI critiques."

Why does Preuve d’atténuation matter in cybersecurity?

Preuve d’atténuation matters because it supports clear communication in Vulnerability Management contexts for SOC Analysts, Security Engineers, and Incident Responders. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as CISSP, CompTIA Security+, and CEH.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, MITRE ATT&CK and published by Protermify Cybersecurity as a static cybersecurity reference page.

Definition

Documented proof that specific technical or administrative actions have effectively addressed and reduced the risk of cryptographic or PKI vulnerabilities, as required by compliance or audit processes.

Operational example

Mitigation evidence, such as updated system logs and compliance checklists, must be retained after critical PKI patches are applied.
